note: The listing is a single-signer row of the founder or a moderate holder, and its cell calls a withdraws of it closing the room. CC 2.4 lets no single signer retire a community. A careful reader takes the cell to mean the listing ends and the room is no longer found; the words say more than that.

side_a: CC 2.4.1.1: "the delegate holds a live `delegates_to` from them, and the kept list binds the delegate as it binds them"
side_b: CC 3.2: "A recovery authority `R` holding `delegates_to(K → R, scope: [owner_binding_recovery])` may sign under rule 4."
note: Rule 3 names the scope its proxy must hold; rule 4 names none, so read alone it lets a delegate under any scope withdraw its principal's rows. CC 3.2 applies rule 4 with a scope that names the act and CC 4.4.3.4.3 says an absent field admits nothing. The rest of the document supports a scope condition the table does not state.

side_a: CC 3.3.1: "Each named party may withdraw ([CC 2.4.1.1](part_2_the_grammar.md) rule 2); only the attester recants"
side_b: data manifests/transitions.tsv: "consent:community_trust withdraw admitted withdrawn author,subject selfAct"
note: The text gives recants to the attester of consent:community_trust and consent:replication and to a trust edge (CC 3.1.1: retracted by withdraws or recants). side_a: CC 3.2: "On the base it is the cosigned `group:roster:v1` row, whose cosigners are the version's signers"
side_b: CC 4.2.6: "The proposal and the participation each sign a distinct, wire-isolated canonical-bytes domain"
note: Text against text. CC 3.2 and the CC 3.1.3 group:roster row make an accord roster version a cosigned row: additional_scrubs over the record's own canonical bytes, reaching the roster-change threshold. CC 4.2.6 has each holder sign an accord_participation preimage (a vote over the proposer's nonce) and says the decision bundle signs nothing. A verifier built from one refuses the roster change the other produces; no sentence says how participations become the version's cosignatures. C051 notes only that the objects are missing from the CC 4.2.1 enumeration.

side_a: CC 4.4.3.2.8: "an act against a member (`membership:removal`, quarantine, slash, a takedown of the member's content) is admitted only when countersigned by a key outside the deciding seat"
side_b: data manifests/family_model.json: "group=affiliations & seats=one => affiliation_member_action@subject_group"
note: Text against data. The affiliation_member_action arm exists on membership:{stage} (leaf removal) and nowhere else. quarantine:{state} and slashing:{outcome} have count none and a one-signer attest; takedown_notice:{basis} has a cosigned case for steward_purge only. A kernel run from the data lets the one deciding seat of an affiliation quarantine, slash or take down a member's content alone, where the text leaves such an act a proposal.

side_a: CC 3.1.9.7: "A member votes for the Goal by cosigning it, and the row is admitted only when its full scrub set meets the group's protocol at `asserted_at`."

side_b: data manifests/transitions.tsv: "mesh_config:{key} attest none admitted steward selfAct"

side_b: CC 3.2: "The founder quorum is never on a timer. The cadence duty is the **witnesses'**."

The three listed consequences are what a node does either way, so the behaviour is the same; the MUST reads as a duty the later sentence denies.

side_a: CC 2.6.5: "Certificate Transparency v2.0 (CT-bis); MUST be used for new transparency-log integrations; older 6962 instances continue to interoperate"
side_b: CC 5.3.3.7: "instantiated per-stream as separate log instances under the same RFC 6962 algorithm"
note: Every normative log statement names RFC 6962 (CC 3.1.2 proofs, CC 5.3.1.1 proof path encoding, per-stream logs), while the references table requires RFC 9162 for new integrations. The Merkle hash is the same; the proof and tree-head encodings are not.

side_a: CC 5.3.6.1: "consistency proof against the prior STH it cosigned is absent or does not verify"
side_b: CC 5.3.1.1: "missing proof when a prior STH exists or a tree_size behind the witness's prior cosigned STH → `MALFORMED_REQUEST`"
note: The error-table cell gives CONSISTENCY_PROOF_INVALID for an absent proof and, in its next sentence, MALFORMED_REQUEST for a missing one. CC 5.3.1.1 gives MALFORMED_REQUEST for missing and the other token only for a proof that does not reconstruct both roots. Two implementers return different tokens for one refusal.

side_a: CC 5.3.1.1: "The Registry MUST reject `POST /v1/transparency/sth/cosign` requests that omit the `consistency_proof_*` fields OR whose consistency proof does not verify against the named prior STH."
side_b: CC 5.3.1.1: "A witness's first cosignature is exempt ("from genesis")."
note: The MUST refuses every request that omits the fields; the next paragraph exempts a witness's first cosignature and refuses a missing proof only when a prior STH exists. A reader of the first paragraph alone refuses a new witness's first cosignature.

side_a: CC 3.3.10.1: "Heads MUST be committed to the [CC 5.4.5](part_5_transport_substrate.md) per-community witness chain at a declared cadence"
side_b: CC 5.4.5: "it is NOT the [CC 5.3.1](#5.3.1) **transparency-log witness** (an independent STH cosigner providing append-only / consistency / anti-equivocation guarantees)"
note: The ledger clause anchors heads against equivocation in the CC 5.4.5 chain, which CC 5.4.5 defines as a privacy discipline and forbids substituting for the anti-equivocation witness. Which witness construction detects a ledger fork cannot be decided from the two sections.

side_a: CC 4.1.5: "downstream `transparency_log:inclusion` from a witness who actually retrieved it"
side_b: CC 3.1.2: "RFC 6962 inclusion proof for an audit leaf."
note: CC 4.1.5 uses the inclusion row as a retriever's attestation of reception, signed by a witness; the registry row is a Merkle inclusion proof with no emitter rule, and the data lets any registered key sign it. One name for two things, and the signer differs.

side_a: CC 2.6.7: "Cosignatures with `signed_at` farther than 5 minutes from the STH's published `signed_at` MUST be rejected."
side_b: data manifests/family_model.json: "receipt future-skew <=5 min, us resolution (check_instant_binding); no W"
note: transparency_log:cosigned:{tree_size} takes the generic freshness cell: judged at receipt, future skew only. The text bounds a cosignature on both sides of the head's own published signed_at, so one dated long before the head is refused by the text and admitted by the cell.

side_a: CC 3.1.2: "Witness-emitted, verify-recognized — emitter rule (`identity_type="witness"`) at CC 3.4.9."
side_b: CC 3.4.10: "`transparency_log:cosigned:*` is reserved: emitter rule is `attesting_key_id` MUST match a `federation_keys` row"
note: A citation: the emitter rule the registry row sends the reader to is in CC 3.4.10 (witness-emitter reservations); CC 3.4.9 is the co-stewarded prefixes. The log-infrastructure sentence of CC 3.4.5 cites CC 3.4.9 for it as well.

side_a: CC 2.4.1: "on any edge carrying `sub_delegation`, `license`, `grant`, `moderate`, `takedown`, `review` or `slash`, or sitting in an affiliation's `hierarchy`"
side_b: data formal/derivation/reaction_text.tsv: "@affiliations expiry required delegation_valid_until default delegation_term_max_secs max charter.role_term from delegation_valid_from"
note: Text against data. The one typed expiry on a delegation (reactions.json, trust:{job}:{version}: required delegation_valid_until, bounded by the term ceiling) is scoped to affiliations. CC 2.4.1 and the CC 2.6.1.7 row require the term, at most 365 days, on every edge that carries an issuance or moderation scope in a group of any kind, and refuse a perpetual or over-ceiling one delegation_term_required. The family's subject_rule cell (code-v61) does say a term is required, so the data disagrees with itself; but run from the reactions, a moderate, takedown, license or grant edge in a family or community has no ceiling and no lapse, and the reaction that locks a room when its moderate edge expires never fires there.

side_a: CC 3.3.4: "A time-boxed guest is a widening with `valid_until`, and the seat lapses at that instant."
side_b: data manifests/reactions.json: ""member": "expires_at","
note: Still present. The only expiry entry of membership:{stage} is the proposal's expires_at; nothing lapses a widening at its valid_until, so a time-boxed guest stays seated. identity:occurrence (CC 4.4.3.4.6) and capacity_assurance:reversible_pending (CC 3.1.2: the binding MUST lapse) still have no expiry entry either.

side_a: CC 3.1.3.1: "A row without `valid_until` is malformed on this family."
side_b: CC 2.6.1.7: "Consumer-policy staleness, independent of expires_at."
note: Still present in part. CC 2.1 now says valid_until is REQUIRED on session:*; the signed-object table of CC 2.6.1.7, which CC 2.1 makes the presence rule, still lists it OPTIONAL as consumer-policy staleness with no family that requires it. The rendezvous route, config:load, emergency mesh_config and the incapacity binding require it too and neither table says so; the data (reactions.json) does.

side_a: CC 3.3.1: "**Substrate-emitted, not subject-emitted** — it records an observed clock event, not a stance"
side_b: data manifests/transitions.tsv: "consent:state:{stance} attest none admitted owner,self selfAct"
note: Still present (also C485). One attest transition with roles owner and self for every leaf: the expired leaf the substrate must emit (reactions.json names identity:substrate_persist) is refused by the role list, and a subject-signed expired row is admitted.

side_a: CC 2.1: "| `expires_at` | `membership:proposal`, REQUIRED |"
side_b: CC 2.6.1.7: "REQUIRED on census:share:{class}:v1 and census:member:share:v1, where it is the period's end (census_return_expired after it)."
note: Still present. CC 2.1 requires expires_at on a membership proposal only; the signed-object table requires it on the two census share rows only; CC 3.1.3 requires it on a lineage_witness proposal and CC 3.1.3.3 makes the 72 hours of a custody report the claim's expires_at. Four places, no one list.

side_a: CC 3.4.12: "require  delegates_to.valid_until <= T2_review_cadence  // no window outruns periodic review;"
side_b: CC 3.4.13: "`delegation_valid_until` is a ceiling, not a renewing timer. Expiry requires a fresh affirmative re-grant."
note: A delegates_to row can carry two instants: the envelope's valid_until (CC 2.1) and delegation_valid_until (CC 2.4.1, the edge's term). The incapacity binding of CC 3.4.12 lapses on the first by name and the guardian's grant of CC 3.4.13 on the second; CC 2.4.1 says a delegation without delegation_valid_until is open-ended. A careful reader follows each section's word, but which member ends a stewardship edge is not said once.
